claim: The LMAO v0.6.0 example adder, assembled with the vendored LMAO of this repository, sums two decimal numbers of up to three digits over its published domain, including carries that overflow to a fourth digit.

newline_divergence.description: The two engines agree on the digits of the sum but not on the trailing newline: the C runner emits one 0x0a more than the Python oracle. This is the EOF/newline semantics difference already known in this repository.

scope_limits: Only the two published input shapes (two "up to 3 digits" numbers, newline separated) are measured.
Negative inputs and non-digit input are out of scope.
The measurement covers the sum; no subtractor or comparator is derived from this run.
example_adder.hell is GPL-3: only the method is reused, never the file, and nothing derived from it enters the MIT core.
not_demonstrated: A borrow-propagating comparator on decimal digits (that is experiment E1).
Whether the same technique fits inside the repository's own byte budget.
license_note: example_adder.hell is GPL-3 (Matthias Lutter, LMAO). Methodology reference only.
